name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft clumped earth with raised clods, gentle lighter dry and darker damp areas and small grit clusters running across tile borders
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-a

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless full-bleed 96x80 texture of clumped earth, with no silhouette, outline, edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or front face. Width is 96 on every row. The column scans show only mottled light and dark clods, grit and damp patches repeating across the tile, with no structural bands. It is a flat top-down terrain texture, which is the expected form for a terrain kind, so it reads as a flat slab with no standing front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown earth field with clumped, mottled variation and no outlines, as expected for a ground tile. It shows 4 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, so it sits between the two. Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no large flat fills. The clods read mostly as soft blotches of mid and dark brown, with few distinct highlight steps, no per-clod shading and little grit detail, so the ramp is closer to 4 steps than the 5-6 Beodeul uses. It has only 6 distinct colours overall, which is a locked-palette effect, but the visible texture is fairly uniform. The raised clods and grit clusters from the brief are only weakly suggested. A careful artist would likely call it a bit flatter than the references, so with doubt it fails.

surfaces.part: seamless earth ground field, uniform texture across all rows

answer.evidence: Full-bleed 96x80 opaque terrain texture with no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical face. Column scans show only mottled earth tones (L 60-118) alternating irregularly down the whole height, with no band structure. It is a flat, seamless ground tile field, so there is no standing object and no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ground patch of the same kind as the grass and paving references. It has about 4 visible tones per tile (about 6 raw colours in total), against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for paving. Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no large flat fills, and the clods and grit clusters run across tile borders. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so any darker edges are tinted brown rather than black. There is no outline in the sticker sense, which fits a ground tile. The weak point is the palette of only 6 colours: the clod shading is a few broad bands with little per-clod highlight or grain, which is thinner than the grass reference's clumped tufts in several greens and the paving's stone-by-stone shading. Visible tones per tile are on par with grass, but the shading ramp is shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps, so I rate density slightly lower. Close, but it would look a bit flatter and more uniform next to the references.
